text: Fisherman'S Wharf-Style Clam Chowder In Bread Bowl

2 tablespoons diced salt pork or 1 slice bacon 1 finely chopped onion 1 finely chopped celery 1 medium potato, peeled and diced 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour 2 cups clam juice 1/4 teaspoon dried thyme 1 cup chopped canned clams 1 cup heavy cream 2 drops Tabasco sauce salt and pepper 1 1/2 lbs bread, bowl

Place salt pork or bacon in a pot and cook 2 minutes over medium heat until crisp. Transfer to a plate and set aside. Add the onion and celery and saute over medium-low heat for 5 minutes or until onions are translucent and celery softens. Sprinkle flour over the mixture and stir into a paste. Add clam juice, potato and thyme. Increase heat and bring ingredients to a boil. Reduce to low and simmer for 15 minutes, or until potatoes are tender. Add clams and stir in cream. Continue to simmer for 5 minutes until thick and creamy. Add salt, pepper and Tabasco sauce. Spoon the chowder into the bread bowl and garnish with salt pork or bacon. Serve hot.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large bowl, combine the salt pork, bacon, onion, celery, thyme, and garlic. Add the flour, Tabascosco sauce, and salt and Pepper. Mix well. Pour the mixture into the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 20 minutes or until the pork is golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool completely.
Serve with a side of chopped celeriacs, chopped parsley, and a side salad.
This recipe is a great way to make a homemade clam chowder. It's a great recipe for a quick and easy dinner.

In a large bowl, combine the salt pork, bacon, onion, celery, potato, flour, clam juice, thyme, and Tabas: mix well. Add the clam juice and cream and mix well, then add the clam mixture and mix. Pour into a greased and floured 13x9-inch baking dish. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large bowl, combine the salt pork, bacon, onion, celery, potato, flour, clam juice, thyme, clams, cream, and sauce. Mix well. Pour into a greased and floured 13x9-inch baking dish. Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 20 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool completely before serving.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the pork, bacon, onion, celery, potato, flour and clam juice. Bring mixture to a simmer and cook until the meat has wilted. Do not overcook. Remove from the heat. Stir in the clam juice, thyme, Worcestershire sauce, Tabas: and 1 1-ounce cream. Stir all of this together and cook gently for 1 hour. Serve with crumbled bread. Garnish each serving with a generous dollop of clams.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the pork, bacon, onion, celery, potato, flour and clam juice. Bring to a steady simmer and cook until the meat has wilted. Do not overcook. Remove from the heat. Stir in the wine, soup, thyme, clams, cream and Tabas: bring to a simmer. Cook until thickened and bubbly. Set aside to cool. Transfer to a small bowl and chill. Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Place all ingredients in a medium bowl. Chill to room temperature. Whisk together flour, clam juice, thyme and clams. Add mixture to bread mixture and toss until well blended. Pour into prepared loaf pans. Bake for 20 minutes.
